# SB-1018 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

## Hazard description
An arc flash event was observed originating from the induction power cabinet feeding the ring rolling induction coils adjacent to the shot blast cabinet. The initiating fault pathway involved energized conductors within the induction power cabinet and a secondary conductive path established by a dislodged grounding lug on the adjacent blast wheel housing. Arc flash hazards include extreme thermal energy, molten metal ejection, overpressure shock, and conductive debris projection. In the observed incident, personnel within the immediate vicinity experienced exposure to intense light and hot particulate; no fatalities occurred, but there were injuries that required medical attention and resulted in lost time. Root cause analysis identified a combination of mechanical loosening and inadequate verification during maintenance as primary contributors to the event.

Background: The induction power cabinet services high-current equipment and is subject to vibration and thermal cycling during normal operation. The shot blast cabinet mounted nearby contains fittings that are periodically removed and reinstalled during maintenance. Fastener retention on the blast wheel liner assembly is therefore a critical interface for maintaining the electrical isolation and mechanical integrity of the blast wheel housing. A specific fastener relating to the blast wheel liner bolt for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) was found to be under-torqued, which allowed relative movement that contributed to a conductive contact path under fault conditions. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.

Step rationale: Ensuring specified fastener torques are applied and documented prevents mechanical loosening that may create unintended conductive paths. Verifying electrical connections and maintaining mechanical interfaces reduces the probability of arcing and limits available fault energy should an event begin. The controls in this bulletin address work practices, mechanical verification, electrical isolation, and record keeping.

## Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet supplying induction coils in the Ring Rolling cell adjacent to the shot blast cabinet. Identified cabinet: EQ-P3-L2-SB01.
- Blast wheel liner and associated fasteners on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01).
- All portable tooling and maintenance access points used during servicing of the induction power cabinet and adjacent shot blast equipment.

Affected personnel: maintenance electricians, mechanical fitters, line operators, and contractors performing work in the P3, line P3-L2 area.

Related procedures: See SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-04, SOP-P3-L2-05 for reference to authorized work methods, lockout-tagout sequences, and permit requirements.

## Required controls
The following controls are mandatory for all work on, or within the immediate zone of influence of, the induction power cabinet and adjacent shot blast equipment.

1. Administrative controls
   - All work on or adjacent to the induction power cabinet requires a pre-job briefing that documents roles, tasks, and hazard controls. The briefing must reference SOP-P3-L2-02 for electrical isolation procedures and SOP-P3-L2-04 for hot work and confined access considerations.
   - Work permits must be issued and retained per SOP-P3-L2-05 for the duration of the job. Permits shall explicitly list the fasteners to be checked and the torque value to be applied to the blast wheel liner bolt for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01).

2. Mechanical verification
   - Before restoring power, verify that all blast wheel liner fasteners are installed and torqued to the specified value. Document application of the specified torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.
   - Use calibrated torque tools. Calibration records for torque equipment must be available at the time of the job and recorded as part of maintenance documentation.

3. Electrical isolation and verification
   - Follow electrical isolation steps in SOP-P3-L2-02. Lockout-tagout must be verified by a qualified electrician and confirmed by a second verifier for critical isolations.
   - Perform voltage verification on the induction power cabinet after isolation and before any conductive contact is made. Document voltage check results on the permit.

4. Work-by-qualified-personnel
   - Only qualified electricians and trained mechanical staff are permitted to perform work within the induction cabinet and on adjacent conductive housings. If contractors are engaged, they must produce training and qualification records before work begins.

5. Zone control and PPE
   - Establish an exclusion zone during energized work; control access and post hazard signage. Enforce PPE appropriate for potential arc flash exposure as determined by site hazard assessment procedures referenced in SOP-P3-L2-04.

6. Post-maintenance inspection and testing
   - After reassembly and prior to energization, inspect all mechanical joints and electrical connectors for correct installation. Record findings and corrective actions.
   - Conduct a controlled re-energization sequence per SOP-P3-L2-02 with a qualified observer and emergency response readiness.

Examples:
- Example 1: During a scheduled bearing replacement on the blast wheel, the liner bolt was removed and reinstalled. The technician applied torque but failed to record the value. Subsequent vibration caused slight loosening; relative movement allowed a conductive contact that coincided with a transient fault from the induction cabinet. Adherence to the requirement to document the applied torque would have flagged the absence of recorded calibration verification and prompted re-checking.
- Example 2: A contractor performed isolation but did not follow the second-verifier requirement in SOP-P3-L2-02. A missed step left a feed energized. The follow-up corrective action included re-training and enforcing the two-verifier confirmation block on the permit.

## Records to keep
- Completed pre-job briefing forms and issued work permits per SOP-P3-L2-05.
- Torque application records showing operator name, torque tool ID, calibration certificate reference, and confirmation of the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) being set to 100 N·m.
- Electrical isolation verification checklists and voltage test results referenced to SOP-P3-L2-02.
- Post-maintenance inspection reports, including any deviations and corrective actions taken.
- Training and qualification records for all personnel who performed the work, including any contractor documentation accepted for the job.

Retention: Records must be filed in the P3 maintenance record system and retained according to site document retention policy as specified in SOP-P3-L2-05.

## Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon release. All activities on the induction power cabinet and adjacent shot blast equipment in P3, line P3-L2 must comply with the controls above before any further work proceeds. Supervisors are responsible for ensuring implementation and for auditing compliance against SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-04, and SOP-P3-L2-05.
